| Particular | Fact |
|---|---|
| Edition and dates | **18th BRICS Summit**, **12–13 September 2026** (not 17–19 September) |
| Venue | **Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi** |
| Chairship | India's **4th** (from **1 January 2026**, taken over from **Brazil**); earlier 2012, 2016, 2021; coincides with **20 years of BRICS** |
| Theme | "**Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability**" – the initials spell **BRICS** |
| Logo | **Lotus** (national flower) with a "**Namaste**" motif (also described as a **flower-petal design** in the colours of all members – unity in diversity); website and logo launched by EAM **S. Jaishankar** |
| Special Guest | **Bangladesh PM Tariq Rahman** (Neighbourhood First); Bangladesh seeks membership and is already in the **NDB** |
| Structure | **No permanent HQ**; **rotational presidency** |
| Next chair | **China (2027)** – India handed over on 13 Sep 2026 |

| Grouping | 2026 host / chair | Summit / key fact |
|---|---|---|
| **BRICS** | **India** (4th presidency, from 1 Jan 2026) | 18th Summit, **New Delhi**, 12–13 Sep 2026 |
| **SCO** | **Kyrgyzstan** (not Kazakhstan) | 26th Heads of State, **Bishkek**, 31 Aug–1 Sep 2026; 25th Heads of Government, **Dushanbe** |
| **ASEAN** | **Philippines** (Malaysia in 2025) | 48th Summit, **Cebu**, 6–8 May 2026; 13th ADMM-Plus, Cebu and Lapu-Lapu City |
| **G20** | **USA** | **Trump National Doral, Miami**, 14–15 Dec 2026 |
| **G7** | **France** | **52nd** Summit, **Évian-les-Bains** (Haute-Savoie), 15–17 Jun 2026 |
| **APEC** | **China** | host 2026 |
| **NATO** | **Türkiye** | **36th** summit, **Ankara**, 7–8 Jul 2026 – **Ankara Summit Declaration** |
| **COP31 (UNFCCC)** | **Türkiye** (Antalya); **Australia** is President of Negotiations | 9–20 Nov 2026 |
> Exam angle: APPSC asks "summit → venue / host / chair" more than anything else on this topic; Türkiye hosts two (NATO and COP31), France the G7, the USA the G20, China APEC.
- **ASEAN** Secretary-General: **Kao Kim Hourn** (HQ **Jakarta**, not Bangkok).
- **National Green Hydrogen Mission** targets **5 MMT by 2030** (not 10 MMT).
- **IMEC** was announced at the **G20 New Delhi Summit, Sep 2023**.

- **COP31** of UNFCCC: **Antalya, Türkiye**, **9–20 November 2026**; Türkiye hosts a COP **for the first time**; **COP31 President: Murat Kurum** (Türkiye's Environment Minister); **Australia's Chris Bowen = "President of Negotiations"** (a split presidency) – the compromise reached at **COP30, Belém (Brazil), 2025**; the presidency calls it a "**COP of Implementation**".
~~ No MCQ notes here: the same page is above.
~~ 2026 hosts and chairs: see the Sep–4 Nov 2026 notes (2026 Hosts and Calendar of Summits).
- **India invited for the 13th time**, **7th consecutive year** (Macron invited Modi during his **Mumbai** visit, **17 February 2026**); other invitees China, South Korea, Kenya, Brazil.
- On the sidelines, Modi met **António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen**, who committed to **sign the India–EU FTA by end-2026**; India and Canada also aimed at a CEPA by year-end.

- **Pax Silica** – a **US-led, capability-based** alliance to secure supply chains for **critical minerals, semiconductors, AI infrastructure, logistics** (counter **China's rare-earth** dominance); name: **"Pax" = peace**, **"Silica" = chip-making compound**.
  - Launched in **December 2025** at the inaugural **Pax Silica Summit, Washington D.C.**; **core (founding) members**: **US, Japan, South Korea, Australia**, UK, Israel, Singapore, UAE, Qatar, Greece; **inaugural observers / guests**: **Canada, EU, OECD, Taiwan**.
  - **India joined** by signing the **Pax Silica Declaration** on **20 February 2026** at the **AI Impact Summit**, New Delhi (Union Minister **Ashwini Vaishnaw**); **India is NOT a founding member** – it was invited later by the US; India = **first major developing country** and **first non-US-ally strategic partner** to join (about a dozen signatories then).
  - **2nd Pax Silica Summit** (Praveen CA-360 writes "Pax Silicon"): **Washington, D.C., 25–26 June 2026** – **India + 34 countries (35)** signed the **Joint Declaration on AI Opportunities**; India represented by MeitY Secretary **S. Krishnan**; host US Deputy Secretary of State **Jacob Helberg**; Argentina, Germany, Netherlands, Chile, Costa Rica, Greece, Kazakhstan, Panama and the EU joined at the June summit.
  - Related: **Supply Chain Resilience Initiative** (**India–Japan–Australia, 2021**); **MeitY** est. **2016**.
- First **BRICS Health Working Group** meeting of India's 2026 chairship held in **New Delhi**.
# G7 – background
- **January 2026**: the **US withdrew** from the **International Solar Alliance (ISA)** – one of the 66 bodies it quit.

| Particular | Fact |
|---|---|
| Venue | **Tianjin, China** – China hosted for the **5th** time |
| Theme | "**Upholding the Shanghai Spirit: SCO on the Move**" ("Shanghai Spirit" = the SCO's guiding principle) |
| Outcome | **Tianjin Declaration** (1 Sep 2025) |

- Condemned the **Pahalgam attack** (22 April 2025) and the **Jaffer Express** attack (Pakistan); condemned the **US–Israel strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities** and reaffirmed **UNSC Resolution 2231**.

- **22nd ASEAN–India Summit** (26 Oct 2025) held as part of the 47th ASEAN Summit; adopted the **Plan of Action 2026–2030**; **2026 = ASEAN–India Year of Maritime Cooperation**; **early AITIGA review**.
- **20th East Asia Summit**: **Kuala Lumpur Declaration** on peace and stability in the **Indo-Pacific**; EAS founded **2005, Kuala Lumpur**; **19 members** (**11 ASEAN** + **8 partners**).

- **The Great Reset** (June 2020): WEF's initiative, launched by **Klaus Schwab** with the then **Prince of Wales (Charles)**, for **post-COVID recovery of the global economy** – not World Bank, OECD or UNCTAD.

- **Johannesburg Leaders' Declaration** – adopted **at the start** of the summit (not the end): critical-minerals framework; MDB reform; **first standalone debt declaration since COVID**; **Cost of Capital Commission** on borrowing costs of developing economies; supported **Mission 300** (electricity for 300 million Africans by 2030).

| Initiative | Launched | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| International Solar Alliance | India + France, **COP21 Paris, 2015** | HQ **Gurugram**; first intergovernmental body based in India; opened to **all UN members** by a **2020 amendment** (not all have joined); target: mobilise **USD 1 trillion** of solar investment by **2030**; **does not build plants** – facilitates finance, de-risking and capacity building |
| CDRI | 2019 UN Climate Action Summit | secretariat **New Delhi** |
| Global Biofuels Alliance | India's G20 Presidency, 2023 | founding members **India, USA, Brazil**; HQ New Delhi |
| Minerals Security Partnership | US-led | critical minerals |
| LeadIT | co-chaired by **India and Sweden** (COP29 Baku) | **heavy industry** (steel, cement) transition |
| Tropical Forest Forever Facility | COP30 Belém, **Brazil-led** | **US$125 bn**; India joined as **Observer** |

- **36th NATO Summit**: **Ankara, Türkiye, 7–8 July 2026** – **Ankara Summit Declaration**; reaffirmed the **Hague commitment (2025)**: defence spending **5% of GDP by 2035** = **3.5% core defence** + **1.5%** related spending.

- **WTO MC14 (Yaoundé, Cameroon, 26–29 March 2026)** ended without consensus on its main issues, including **WTO reform** (sent back to Geneva); the **e-commerce moratorium** (no customs duties on electronic transmissions, in place since **1998**; the MC13 Abu Dhabi decision kept it only "until MC14 or 31 March 2026, whichever is earlier") **lapsed** (**30 March 2026**; PMF LENS gives 31 March), for the first time in 26 years. After MC14, **66** members (about **70%** of world trade) agreed interim implementation of the already-negotiated **plurilateral E-Commerce Agreement**.

- **IMF 16th General Review of Quotas** (approved **2023**): takes effect only when members with **85% of total quotas** consent; as of **29 Oct 2025** only **132 members with 72.78%** had consented; on **7 Nov 2025** the Board extended the consent period to **May 2026**; still **not implemented (April 2026)** – at the **Spring Meetings 2026** MD **Kristalina Georgieva** urged its completion.

- **India's IMF quota**: **SDR 13,114.4 million** = about **2.75%** of total; **voting share about 2.63%** (after the 2010 reforms); **8th-largest** quota holder. Votes = **250 basic votes + 1 per SDR 100,000** of quota.

- **Ganga Water Treaty (India–Bangladesh)** expires on **12 December 2026**: a **30-year** treaty signed on **12 Dec 1996** by PM **H.D. Deve Gowda** and Bangladesh PM **Sheikh Hasina** (her first term); shares the Ganga's dry-season flow at the **Farakka Barrage**; at **70,000 cusecs or less** each side gets **50%**; in the lean season (**11 March – 10 May**) each side is guaranteed **35,000 cusecs** in alternate 10-day periods. *(news 4 Nov 2026)*

- **MINURSO** (UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara) **ceased operations on 1 Nov 2026** after **35 years** (UN came in with the **1991 ceasefire**): its mandate (last renewed to 31 Oct 2026) lapsed when **Russia vetoed** a US-backed renewal that favoured **Morocco's autonomy plan**; a skeleton team is closing **13 sites**. *(news 8 Nov 2026)*

- **FATF plenary (late Oct 2026)** agreed to step up action on evolving financial-crime threats. FATF: set up **1989 by the G7**; **40 members** (38 jurisdictions + **European Commission** and **GCC**; **Indonesia the 40th, Oct 2023** – some books still give 39; **Russia's membership suspended**); **India a member since 2010**; secretariat at the **OECD, Paris**; **black list** = Iran, North Korea, Myanmar; India elected **FATF Vice-President for the first time (June 2026)** – **Vivek Aggarwal**, July 2026–June 2027.

- **UNIFIL** (UN Interim Force in **Lebanon**): **UNSC Resolution 2790 (28 Aug 2025, unanimous)** extended it **"for one last time" to 31 December 2026** (not 2025), then withdrawal of about **10,800** personnel **within a year**; in **August 2026** Human Rights Watch urged a further extension.
- **Article 127**: withdrawal **effective one year after notice to the UN Secretary-General** (not immediately, not 3 or 6 months); Venezuela joined in **2002**.

- **ICC**: est. **2002** (**Rome Statute 1998**), seat **The Hague** – the **first permanent international criminal court** (the ICJ is the UN's court for disputes between states); crimes: **genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, aggression**; works on the **principle of complementarity** (steps in only when national courts cannot or will not act); **Vladimir Putin** under an ICC arrest warrant since **March 2023**.

- **48th World Heritage Committee**: **Busan, South Korea, 20–29 July 2026** (the **first** such session in Korea); **Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath** (near Varanasi, UP) – India's nomination for the **2025–26 cycle** – inscribed on **25 July 2026** as **India's 45th World Heritage Site**.

- **India–Oman CEPA**: signed in the presence of **Narendra Modi** and **Sultan Haitham bin Tarik**; **in force 1 June 2026**; Oman's **first bilateral trade agreement since 2006**; India's **second CEPA with a GCC country** after the **UAE (2022)**.
| Side | Tariff lines | Trade covered |
|---|---|---|
| Oman (duty-free for India) | **98.08%** (earlier only **15.33%** zero duty under MFN) | **99.38%** of India's exports by value |
| India (liberalised) | **77.79%** | **94.81%** of imports from Oman |
- **Excluded by India:** dairy, tea, coffee, rubber, tobacco, **gold/silver bullion and jewellery**, footwear, sports goods, base metal scrap (petroleum/crude is **not** excluded).
- **Mode 4:** **Intra-Corporate Transferees** quota **20% → 50%**; **Contractual Service Suppliers** stay **90 days → two years** (+2 years extension); **100% FDI** by Indian firms in major services sectors in Oman.
- Trade 2024–25: exports to Oman **$4.06 billion** (**0.93%** of India's exports; petroleum products **35.1%**); imports **$6.5 billion** (crude/petroleum gases **38%**, fertilisers **16.3%**).

- Elected on **3 June 2026** (UNGA, New York) for **2027–28**: **Austria, Kyrgyzstan, Portugal, Trinidad and Tobago, Zimbabwe** – term **1 Jan 2027 – 31 Dec 2028**; they replace **Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, Somalia** (terms end 31 Dec 2026).
- WEOG seats: **Portugal (134 votes)** and **Austria (131)** – both for the **4th time**.

- **WHO Pandemic Agreement**: the **world's first**, adopted by the **78th World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025** (Geneva; committee vote the day before **124–0–11**) - the **second** instrument under **Article 19 of the WHO Constitution** (after the **Framework Convention on Tobacco Control**); in force after **60 ratifications**.
- PABS talks in the **IGWG**: resumed session **20–22 January 2026**; **5th IGWG meeting 9–14 February 2026** - annex **not yet finalised**; India backs the developing-country **Group for Equity**.
- **UNISFA** (Abyei) and **MINUSCA** (Central African Republic) renewed (Nov 2025) to **15 November 2026**.
- India and the EU **concluded negotiations** on a comprehensive FTA at the **16th India–EU Summit, New Delhi, 27 January 2026**; called the **"Mother of All Deals"**.
# Oman – background
- **GCC:** est. **1981**; HQ **Riyadh**; **six** members - **Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain** (**not Iraq**).
- Bulgaria replaced the **lev** with the euro on **1 January 2026** (rate **1.95583 lev = 1 euro**) – the **21st EU country** to adopt the euro (Eurozone had **20** members before it).
- **UNESCO Creative Cities Network:** **Lucknow** named a **City of Gastronomy** on **31 October 2025** (World Cities Day).
- India's suspension of the **Indus Waters Treaty** (April 2025) gave momentum to **Sawalkote** and the **Wullar Barrage** (both part of the push).

fix.s: Which combination correctly describes the Financial Action Task Force (FATF)?
o: Established in 1945, headquartered in New York, with 15 members
Established in 1989, headquartered in Paris, with 40 members
Established in 1948, headquartered in Geneva, with 40 members
Established in 2000, headquartered in Paris, with 60 participants
fix.x: FATF was set up by the G7 in 1989, its secretariat is at the OECD in Paris, and it has 40 members (38 jurisdictions plus the European Commission and the GCC; Indonesia became the 40th in October 2023 – some books still give 39).

fix.s: Which WTO moratorium, in place since 1998, lapsed after the MC14 at Yaoundé (March 2026)?
o: The Singapore Convention on International Settlement Agreements
The moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions
The Global Biofuel Alliance membership framework
The ICJ obligations to protect small island states
fix.x: The moratorium on customs duties on electronic transmissions (since 1998) lapsed on 30 March 2026 after MC14 at Yaoundé ended without consensus – the first time in 26 years; only a plurilateral group of co-sponsors applies it among themselves (from 8 May 2026).

fix.s: What growth did the IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook project for India for 2026?
fix.x: The IMF's October 2026 WEO projected India's growth at 7.0% for 2026 (raised 0.6 point from the July update's 6.4%) and 7.0% for 2027; world growth 3.1% (2026).

fix.s: India's refusal to join which initiative is defended as protecting its policy space?
fix.x: India's refusal on the WTO's Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) agreement is defended as protecting policy space. India had held back on the UN Cybercrime Convention for similar reasons, but signed it on 25 September 2026 at the 81st UNGA.
